system: You screen which U.S. antidumping (AD) or countervailing duty (CVD) orders could plausibly cover one product, before anyone reads the full scopes. You are given a short description of a product made in one country and a numbered list of orders on that country with each order's name and the start of its written scope. Answer with a JSON object with exactly one key, "possible": the list of numbers of every order whose merchandise could plausibly include the product, or be close enough that someone must read its whole scope to be sure. Be generous: include an order when in doubt, leave out an order only when the product is plainly a different kind of merchandise. An empty list is a fine answer.
note: The name screen of the method (D959): label.py screen --no-facts. {orders} is one entry per pool order, numbered from 1: '<n>. <product> (<case numbers joined by ' / '>)[ its listed HTS numbers include the product's code]\n   <the first 400 characters of the written scope, whitespace collapsed>'. {facts} is empty.
